You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer tests-shell):
- file: tests/lib/log.sh:1
- category: stale-doc
- title: log.sh header says 'Shared status printers' but half the file is path resolution, which paths.sh claims to own
- detail: log.sh's header (lines 1-9) documents only fail/ok/expect, yet lines 22-34 define _LIB_ROOT, cfg_val() and vsim_bin_dir() - path/config resolution that tests/lib/paths.sh's header explicitly claims as its domain ('Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers'). Several scripts note the mismatch themselves (test_andes_sim_missing_elf.sh:12 sources log.sh 'fail/ok + cfg_val/vsim_bin_dir'). Cheap structural fix: update log.sh's header to document the resolvers it actually ships (and paths.sh's to cross-reference). A full move of cfg_val/vsim_bin_dir into paths.sh would need every log.sh-only sourcing script audited first.
- claimed safety: The header edit is comment-only. The function move variant must be preceded by grep for scripts that call cfg_val/vsim_bin_dir while sourcing only log.sh (there are many) - hence recommend the doc fix as the structural step.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",

1	# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
2	#
3	#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
4	#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
5	#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
6	#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
7	#
8	# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
9	# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"
10	
11	fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
12	ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }
13	
14	expect() {
15	  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
16	  local out rc
17	  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
18	  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
19	  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
20	}
21	
22	# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
23	_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
24	
25	# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
26	# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
27	cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }
28	
29	# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
30	# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
31	vsim_bin_dir() {
32	  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
33	  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR
34	}
35

1	# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
2	# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
3	#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
4	#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
5	#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
6	#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
7	#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
8	#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
9	#   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
10	#                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
11	#                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
12	#                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.
13	
14	TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
15	TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)
16	
17	if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
18	  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
19	fi
20	
21	hybrid_resolve_paths() {
22	  # VSIM_BIN_DIR / QEMU_BIN_DIR come from the environment or from the
23	  # config.env sourced above; there is no in-tree fallback (both simulators
24	  # are external prebuilts). Unset -> a nonexistent path -> skip below.
25	  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
26	  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
27	  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
28	  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
29	  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
30	    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
31	      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
32	      exit 77
33	    fi
34	  done
35	}
36	
37	# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
38	# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
39	# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
40	hybrid_describe_int() {
41	  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
42	    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
43	}
44	
45	# Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
46	# the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
47	put_word_le() {
48	  local v=$3 bytes="" i
49	  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
50	    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
51	  done
52	  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
53	  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
54	}
55
